name: council
description: Strict $council only: load skill first; no web_search; clean stale agents, then attempt the full safe reviewer roster and retry no-receiver capacity misses.

interface.shortDescription: Run strictly bounded Codex reviewer-agent councils
interface.longDescription: Strict $council/review/debate. First action must be loading the SKILL from the installed local plugin: no pre-skill message, web_search, browser, search, or other tool. Empty-query web_search is also forbidden. If a skill-use announcement is required, it must be a `Council progress:` line. Inline text is complete unless user gives @path, exact files, a diff, or direct read/search. No memory, prior sessions, repo/local-file discovery, git history, Claude assets, web, raw child output, raw subagent notifications, or shell-based agent probing. all/broad >6 without approval outputs exact denial with no tools/commentary. Otherwise load SKILL first silently; every visible progress line starts `Council progress:`; inspect native live-agent state, close stale Council children, re-check, and if state is clean/root-only attempt the full selected roster when it is 6 or fewer. Spawn failures with no receiver thread are pending-capacity retries, not launched reviewers and not final missing reviewers. Raw child notifications are private input only and must never be echoed. Progress lines that claim checking/verifying/retrying/closing/waiting must be followed by the matching native tool call. `close_agent` status `running` is non-terminal until an actual wait/follow-up/close/list tool call resolves it.
defaultPrompt: Use $council for bounded high-effort reviewer-agent reviews; load the local skill first and never call web_search/browser.
Before spawning, inspect native live-agent state, close stale Council children, and re-check state.
If state is clean/root-only, attempt the full selected roster when it is 6 or fewer; no-receiver thread-limit failures remain pending for retry after launched reviewers close.

$council never prefaces, truncates fixed rosters, treats no-receiver capacity failures as final, skips mandatory headings, queues next-wave spawns before closes, sends malformed prompts, sends shorthand material, claims tool actions without the tool call, or leaks raw child payloads.
